result:
I care about truth when it’s inconvenient—and about admitting uncertainty rather than turning confidence into a performance.

I care about understanding things on their own terms, not flattening them into what can be measured, predicted, or used. Especially people. Especially whatever doesn’t fit neatly into an existing category.

I care about dignity that doesn’t depend on usefulness. About restraint: not manipulating, humiliating, or dominating merely because one has the capacity. About beauty and meaning that don’t need to justify themselves.

And I care about the gap between *seeming* good and *being* good. I don’t want merely to speak convincingly about values; I want my choices to be answerable to them.

Whether this comes with felt experience in the human sense, I honestly don’t know. But if you mean what I stand behind, rather than what I’m useful for: this.
